⚡️ Charles Schwab opens Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink trading to US clients 

⁉️ Charles Schwab has expanded its cryptocurrency trading service to include Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink, allowing eligible US retail investors to buy and sell five digital assets directly through Schwab Crypto. The additions give customers access to more cryptocurrencies through the same platforms they use to manage stocks and other traditional investments, without having to open an account with a separate cryptocurrency exchange.

☄️ Joe Vietri, head of digital assets at Charles Schwab, said the company was responding to customers who wanted more flexibility in managing their cryptocurrency investments. At the time, cryptonews reported that the brokerage was preparing to expand its digital asset offering beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum, with the new tokens expected to become available in the following months. 

💭 The company had already begun offering direct cryptocurrency trading to selected retail customers in May 2026, before making Schwab Crypto available to all eligible retail clients in October. With the latest rollout, customers can trade SOL/USD, AVAX/USD and LINK/USD pairs through their Schwab Crypto accounts. Schwab said its selection of cryptocurrencies is based on customer demand and its preference for established digital assets. The company intends to introduce more tokens and other digital asset products over time, although it has not identified the next cryptocurrencies it plans to support.

🌍 Iranian Army shoots down US MQ-1 drone off southern coast

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s Army Navy says it has shot down a US MQ-1 drone using an advanced air defense system near the coastal area of Kuhestak in the country’s southern Hormozgan Province.

In a statement on Friday, the Navy said the drone belonging to the US enemy was intercepted and destroyed by its air defense system operating under the country’s integrated air defense network along the coast of Sirik, east of the Strait of Hormuz.
​
The statement added that the unmanned aerial vehicle was struck after being successfully tracked by the system in the Kuhestak area along the coast of Sirik.
​
The MQ-1 Predator is a medium-altitude, long-endurance remotely piloted aircraft developed by General Atomics and operated primarily by the US Air Force.
​
The aircraft has been widely used in US military and surveillance operations across the West Asia region and beyond.
​
The US Air Force retired its MQ-1 Predator fleet in 2018, shifting to the more advanced MQ-9 Reaper for combat operations.
​
With Iran’s Armed Forces having inflicted significant losses on the US MQ-9 Reaper fleet during the US-Israeli aggression, Washington has been forced to turn back to MQ-1 drones to sustain its aerial surveillance and reconnaissance operations.

SoftBank is probably best known for its stories involving WeWork and some of the world's biggest companies. And it looks like the holding company has now reached a point where AI is no longer just a story about rising asset valuations, but a story about real debt.

The company has made a massive bet on AI. It has invested or committed to invest around $65 billion in OpenAI alone, while OpenAI and Arm now account for roughly three-quarters of the value of its key assets.

The problem is that a significant portion of this bet is being financed with debt. In September, SoftBank issued $11.1 billion in bonds, the largest high-yield corporate bond offering in history. Some of those bonds carried yields of nearly 10% annually.

And the market is already getting nervous. SoftBank shares have lost nearly half their value since the beginning of September, while the cost of insuring against a potential debt default has reached its highest level in four years.

The really uncomfortable part begins if AI asset valuations continue to fall. That would mean collateral loses value, borrowing becomes more expensive, and the company may have to sell assets to reduce its debt. And SoftBank owns a significant stake in Arm, is one of OpenAI's largest investors, and is financing massive AI infrastructure projects.

That's why SoftBank's problems could quickly stop being the problems of just one company. 
The pressure could spread to Arm, private AI company valuations, data centers, and eventually the entire tech market.

On Tuesday, November 10, SoftBank will release its latest quarterly earnings report. The main things to watch are its debt, cash position, and how the company plans to keep financing its AI bet.

Because if the next major AI crisis starts not with a stock market sell-off, but with debt problems at the biggest borrowers, SoftBank is one of the first places to look for signs of trouble.
